subject: Mutual action plan and capacity timing for HelioHealth (Dedicated -> Private path)
body:
From: Sam Wright <sam.wright@heliohealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 10:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP and timeline questions

Hey Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — team liked the latency profiles, especially warm-cache numbers. We need a concrete mutual action plan that ties evaluation gates to capacity commitments so procurement has something to budget toward. Two questions up front: 1) for Dedicated -> Private path, what are the realistic lead times for H100 and A100 pools? 2) how granular should we size tranches for a 9-month ramp (pilot -> prod)?

Can you send a sample MAP with milestones and rough capacity ranges so we can align with finance?

Best,
Sam
Sr. Platform Architect, HelioHealth

----

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Sam Wright <sam.wright@heliohealth.com>, procure@heliohealth.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP and timeline questions

Sam — great to hear. I attached a first-pass MAP and a capacity estimate that shows three tranche options (conservative / target / aggressive). High-level answers: 1) Dedicated H100 pools (hosted reserved) — plan for a 10–14 week lead time from signed commit to first usable slice if hardware is available; Private/on-prem procurement tends to be 16–22 weeks due to racks, networking, and on-site acceptance. 2) For a 9-month ramp I recommend 3 tranches: pilot (10–20% of target), scale (50–60%), and full (remaining). Each tranche has a 6–8 week evaluation window to validate latency, token economics, and KV cache behavior.

Attachments: HelioHealth_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP draft), capacity_estimate_v2.pdf (GPU sizing by tranche)

Proposed next steps in the MAP:
- Week 0: NDA & SOW sign (we set procurement template in parallel)
- Weeks 1–6: Pilot evaluation on Dedicated (small tranche, H100-rt instances)
- Weeks 7–12: Performance gating; if pass -> commit tranche 2 and begin Private prep
- Weeks 13–22: Private provisioning (if chosen) + canary traffic to Private cluster
- Weeks 23–36: Full capacity activation and tuning (quantization & batching profiles)

I called out acceptance gates (latency 99p, cost/unit delta, regression-free outputs) in the MAP. Happy to refine after a quick call.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

----

From: Sam Wright <sam.wright@heliohealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 08:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP and timeline questions

Ben — this is exactly what I needed. Couple clarifications:
- On the Dedicated lead time, does the 10–14 weeks assume available H100 inventory globally or region-specific pools?
- For Private prep, can you break out the major acceptance checkpoints (networking, KMS, SOC evidence) we need before commit tranche 2?

Procurement here is looking for a conservative cost estimate tied to each tranche so we can run scenario planning. Can your team add a tranche-level peg (token/unit cost) to the capacity_estimate_v2?

I'll loop in procurement if needed.

—Sam

----

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Sam Wright <sam.wright@heliohealth.com>, procure@heliohealth.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP and timeline questions

Sam — quick update with attachments and internal asks. Replied inline below and added a short internal note I circulated to ops to confirm lead-time assumptions.

Inline:
- Dedicated 10–14 weeks: this assumes availability in the US-west region (we align inventory at commit). If Helio needs a strict calendar date across multiple regions, add a 4–6 week buffer for cross-region sourcing.
- Private prep acceptance checkpoints (we'll provide a readiness checklist):
  * Week A (Network): IP allocation, routing table, firewall rules, VPN/DirectConnect tests
  * Week B (Security): KMS integration, role-based access control, audit log forwarding to your SIEM
  * Week C (Compliance): SOC2 evidence package, data retention policy agreement, optional on-site audit window
  * Week D (Acceptance): Performance runbook, smoke tests, canary traffic plan, rollback criteria

- Tranche-level token/unit cost: attached capacity_estimate_v2.pdf now includes conservative/target/aggressive per-token cost assuming batching and quantization profiles. See tab 'Cost Pegs'.

Attachments: HelioHealth_MAP_v1.xlsx (updated), capacity_estimate_v2.pdf (updated), nda_helio.pdf

Internal note to ops (forwarded below):

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: HelioHealth — validate lead times + acceptance checkpoints

Priyom / Lauren — can you confirm the following by EOD Monday:
1) H100 availability assumption for US-west (is 10–14 weeks realistic if we secure a tranche on signing?)
2) Private deployment 16–22 weeks: list the critical path items and estimated durations for networking, rack install, and on-site acceptance
3) Any known SOC2 evidence lag that would extend Private acceptance?

Summary for ops: Helio is asking for a MAP that ties evaluation gates to tranche commit decisions. We want to be conservative on lead times in the MAP but still show an aggressive timeline they can aim for.

Thanks — Ben
